name: passkey-sign-in
title: Passkey sign-in
description: A passkey-first sign-in: one large "Sign in with a passkey" button, autofill on the email field, and a quiet fallback to a password or a link.
docs: onPasskey({ email }) is yours: run WebAuthn in it (the block never touches navigator.credentials) and resolve when it is done; email is what was typed in the field and may be empty. While the browser prompt is open the big button reads Waiting for your device with a spinner and the same press cannot run twice (busy forces that state for a redirect or a preview). Report what went wrong through error: cancelled, not-found or unsupported each become plain words with the next step, announced once (a rejection with no error set shows a general message; labels.errors translates them). supported={false} removes the button and the field and leads with the fallbacks as full buttons. fallbacks are { id, label, href or onSelect }, shown as quiet text actions under the field (Use a password instead, Email me a link). The email field has autocomplete=username webauthn, so the browser can offer a saved passkey in it, and pressing Enter in it runs the same sign-in. A one-line explanation of what a passkey is sits behind a term, the word passkey with a dotted underline that opens a small named panel on click, tap or Enter (labels.lead, term and definition). Targets are 44px and up (the word passkey is a link inside a sentence, with a padded hit area), the fingerprint tile is a monochrome circle, and nothing depends on a pointer. titleAs sets the heading element, footer sits under the card.
